summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biography of Jacob C. Higgins (1826–1893), a Pennsylvania commander who served in both the Mexican–American War and the American Civil War. It highlights his command of the 125th Pennsylvania Infantry at the battles of Antietam and Chancellorsville, and his organization of Emergency Militia that countered a Confederate cavalry threat to Altoona and the Juniata River watershed during the Gettysburg Campaign.
one_line: Biography of Jacob C. Higgins, a Pennsylvania commander in the Mexican–American and Civil wars who organized militia against a Gettysburg-era Confederate raid.
key_facts: Jacob C. Higgins lived from 1826 to 1893.
Jacob C. Higgins was a native commander of Pennsylvania troops.
Jacob C. Higgins took part in both the Mexican–American War and the American Civil War.
Jacob C. Higgins guided the 125th Pennsylvania Infantry regiment under heavy fire at the Battle of Antietam.
The Battle of Antietam is described in the note as the 'Bloodiest Day in American History'.
Jacob C. Higgins guided the 125th Pennsylvania Infantry under heavy fire at the Battle of Chancellorsville on May 3, 1863.
May 3, 1863 is described in the note as the 'Second Bloodiest Day of the Civil War'.
During the Gettysburg Campaign, Confederate General John D. Imboden led cavalry to threaten vital railroad resources at Altoona.
The Confederate cavalry under John D. Imboden also threatened iron production facilities in the Juniata River watershed.
Emergency Militia was organized by Colonel Jacob C. Higgins after the 125th PA was mustered out and returned home.
The Emergency Militia organized by Colonel Higgins minimized the Confederate northwestern incursion.
The 125th Pennsylvania Infantry was mustered out and returned home before the Gettysburg Campaign incursion.
